To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the light harvesting chloroplasts of the duckweed Spirodela oligorhiza contain two distinct types of thylakoid membrane, granal and stroma lamellae.

the apoproteins for the light harvesting chlorphyll a/b complex, the 32 kilodal ton protein of PSII, the D2 and cytochrome 559 proteins of PSII, and subunit 1 protein of PSI are dually located between grana and stroma lamellae.

the apoproteins and reaction center components of PSI and PSII are dually localized, while the 43 and the 51 kilodaltons proteins of PSII, the alpha and the beta subunits of ATPase are exclusively located in the granal and stromale lamellae, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lateral distribution of the major proteins of thylakoid membranes in Spirodela oligorrhiza.
the distribution of thylakoid membrane proteins between stromal and granal lamellæ in Spirodela oligorhiza.
the distribution of thylakoid components between granal and stroma thylakoid lamellae in Spirodelan cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PSII components are localized to the granal lamellalike membranes of the thylakoid, whereas PSI components and light-harvesting complex apoproteins are localized to both granal and stromalemma-like membranes.
all of the proteins examined are distributed between stromal and granal lamellate membranes, but with the majority of each protein in one lamellar fraction or the other.
the thylakoid membrane is a continuum of protein composition and not a discrete mosaic of two types of protein complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PSII reaction-center proteins and the light-harvesting proteins are dually located between grana and stromal lamella, while the PSII 43- and 51-kilodalton proteins and the ATPase subunits are localized exclusively in the grana and stromae, respectively.

PSI components were localized in stromal lamellar membranes and PSII components in granal lamellar membranes, with the exception that the PSII reaction-center components, the D2 and cytochrome proteins, and the light-harvesting chlorophyll a/ b complex apoproteins were distributed between granal and stroma lamellae.

the PSII reaction-center proteins are located in the stroma-exposed regions of thylakoids, and that the PSI reaction-center proteins and the light-harvesting chlorophyll a /b protein are located in the grana-exposed regions of the membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral distribution of thylakoid components in Spirodela is not completely segregated, but is rather a continuum between the two lamellar types.
, in contrast to higher plants, the PSI and PSII complexes of Spirodela are not completely separated in the thylakoid membrane.
PSII components are not restricted to granal lamellare, and this finding has significant implications for the mechanism of photosynthesis in vivo and the interpretation of in vitro experiments.
